parameters.content:
## 1 — MCP surface
These three tools are what an MCP client (Claude) sees.
`find_available_slots` runs the whole engine below in a single call, so the model never does date maths itself.

parameters.name: find_available_slots
parameters.description: Returns bookable meeting slots already filtered against the user's calendar AND against prayer times (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, plus a wide Jumu'ah window on Fridays), with buffers around existing meetings. ALWAYS call this before book_meeting. Never invent a time — only offer times present in the returned `slots` array.

value.date: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('date', 'The day to check, format YYYY-MM-DD. Leave empty to scan the next working days.', 'string', "") }}
value.duration_minutes: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('duration_minutes', 'How long the meeting should be, in minutes.', 'number', 30) }}
value.days_to_scan: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('days_to_scan', 'How many days ahead to scan. Leave 0 unless the user asked for a range — 0 means one day when a date is given, otherwise the next few working days.', 'number', 0) }}

parameters.toolDescription: Books a meeting on the user's calendar and creates a Google Meet link. Only use start/end values that came back from find_available_slots. Times must be full ISO 8601 with the +03:00 offset.

additionalFields.description: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('agenda', 'Agenda or notes for the invite body.', 'string', "") }}
attendees: ={{ /*n8n-auto-generated-fromAI-override*/ $fromAI('attendee_emails', 'Comma separated email addresses of the guests.', 'string', "") }}

parameters.toolDescription: Lists everything already on the user's calendar from the start of today through the next 7 days. Use it to answer 'what does my day look like' or to double-check a booking that was just made.

parameters.content:
## 2 — Availability engine
`find_available_slots` re-enters the workflow here.
Calendar events and prayer times are gathered, then **Compute Slots** subtracts busy blocks, prayer windows and buffers from the working day and returns only slots that survive.

parameters.jsCode:
// ── One item per day, so the prayer-times request runs once per day ──
return $('Prep Request').first().json.days.map(d => ({ json: d }));
